anomalies.observed: All VDD supply pins on both MCUs are listed on unconnected nets. The regulator output is on +3.3V, while the separate +3V3 net is not joined to it.
anomalies.expected: Both MCUs' VDD pins should receive the regulated 3.3 V rail, as the specification says the 3.3 V rail feeds both MCUs.

evidence.quote: 3.3V feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Neither MCU has its required VDD supply connected, so the flight-control computers cannot operate. The apparent 3.3 V regulator output also does not connect to the distinct +3V3 net.

anomalies.observed: The two FCC1 pins identified as VCAP are connected directly to the UART3 connector; the 2.2 µF capacitor C13 has an unconnected first pad.
anomalies.expected: VCAP pins should have the required local capacitor connection and should not be used as UART signals; UART3 should use MCU UART-capable signal pins.
anomalies.impact: The H753 internal-core supply bypass requirement is not met, and the UART3 connector is wired to VCAP rather than UART signals. This can prevent reliable MCU operation and makes UART3 unusable.

anomalies.observed: The FCC crystal is connected to FCC1 PE6/PE7 rather than its PH0/PH1 oscillator pins; those PH pins instead connect to a capacitor and the VREF+ network. The NAVC crystal nets do not connect to NAVC1, while NAVC1 PH0/PH1 connect to capacitors to ground.
anomalies.expected: The specified 25 MHz HSE crystals should connect to the HSE input/output pins of their respective MCUs.
anomalies.impact: Neither MCU has the specified 25 MHz crystal correctly connected to its HSE pins, so the intended external clock source will not operate.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows multiple functional wiring faults: both MCUs lack VDD connections, FCC VCAP pins are repurposed as UART3 signals, and neither HSE crystal is correctly connected to its MCU. These deviations would prevent normal operation of the flight-control system.
